precepts.text: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; Saul had two chances to repent and confess and still justified himself, so Samuel did exactly what the scripture says and rejected him.
precepts.point: Samuel refuses: I will not return with thee; for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel. Think it through: Samuel gave Saul the opening at the bleating of the sheep, and Saul would not humble down; he asked why Saul disobeyed the voice of the Lord, and Saul justified himself again. Two admonitions were given and refused before this rejection.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.” Think it through. Samuel gave Saul the opening at the bleating of the sheep, and Saul would not humble down; he asked why Saul disobeyed the voice of the Lord, and Saul justified himself again. Two admonitions were given and refused before this rejection.

“A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject”. Saul had two chances to repent and confess and still justified himself, so Samuel did exactly what the scripture says and rejected him.

precepts.point: They are reprobate. It is impossible to repent after that.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
“A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.” Once they go to heresy and do not want to repent, after the first and second admonition the heretic is rejected. The Most High will take away their spirit.

They are reprobate, and it is impossible to repent after that. So Paul says of whoever preaches another gospel, “let him be accursed”: there is nothing left to do with a heretic but reject him.

points: Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work. Now some of you might not like that verse. It is telling you, like Romans 13, obey the powers that be — obey the laws of the land. If we do not bring stuff like that out, you will be like that young boy we saw cursing out the cops after he stole the brandy, and then you get knocked upside the head. And now your parents want to know why your child was acting up.

We never say all police are good — some of them are no damn good. But you have got to teach your kids to obey the powers that be and keep the laws of the land, as long as they do not contradict God's laws.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men. When it says speak evil of no man, that is talking about gossip.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain. Brothers, when we are teaching, we're not there to convince anybody of anything, and we're not there to argue. Arguing will not win a soul; debating will not win a soul. We are there to teach. Whether they accept it or not is up to Messiah. We are there to plant that seed.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject. Don't argue back and forth: reject. Once you put the law down and they don't want to hear it, that's it; you got to go. Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures: bitterness is one of those lusts. Living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another: when you have the root of bitterness you are literally living in malice. Do not be a hater; stop the hate. We learned that spirit here in this captivity.
